title: Ideal gas law

items.label: P
items.meaning: pressure of the gas (units must match the units of R, e.g. atm)

items.label: V
items.meaning: volume of the gas (units must match the units of R, e.g. L)

items.label: n
items.meaning: amount of gas in moles, which can come from stoichiometric mole ratios

items.label: R
items.meaning: ideal gas constant (its units must match the P and V units used)

caution: Temperature must be in kelvin. Use the value of R whose units match your P and V. The law treats the gas as ideal.
ced_evidence: 4.5.A.3: "Stoichiometric calculations can be combined with the ideal gas law"

title: Molarity

items.label: M
items.meaning: molarity, the concentration of solute in mol/L

items.label: V
items.meaning: volume of the solution in liters (not volume of solvent)

caution: V is the total volume of solution in liters. Convert mL to L before calculating.
ced_evidence: 4.5.A.3: "calculations involving molarity to quantitatively study gases and solutions"; 4.6.A.1: "The titrant has a known concentration"
